chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Khazzaz, from Ali ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Kuleyb Al-Saydawi who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Striking the drumsticks grows hypocrisy in the heart just as water grows vegetation.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual effect of music on the heart according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the physical act of playing music, specifically striking the drumsticks, actively cultivates hypocrisy (nifaq) within the heart, employing a vivid botanical analogy to water nurturing vegetation. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is interpreted not merely as a passive state but as an active spiritual process where the rhythmic engagement with music erodes sincerity, leading to a duality between outward appearance and inner faith. This hadith serves as a foundational text in the jurisprudence of music, linking aesthetic pleasure directly to moral and spiritual decay.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Khazzaz, from Ali Bin Abdul Rahman, from Kuleyb Al Saydawi who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Striking the two drumsticks grows the hypocrisy in the heart just as the water grows the vegetation’.
en.sarwar: 20. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ali ibn Ma‘bad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz from Ali ibn ‘ Abd al- Rahman from Kulayb al-Saydawiy who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
Playing ‘Ud (a certain musical instrument) grows hypocrisy just as water grows green plants.’”
